newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour would veto more EU majority voting.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour would veto more EU majority voting.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour Party would veto any extension of majority voting on matters covered by the European Union's social chapter, finance spokesman Gordon Brown said on Monday.

Brown said he would use a speech later on Monday to the Confederation of British Industry employers' group to make clear that his party would adopt "a balanced and moderate approach to implementation of the social chapter".
Brown's comments were clearly designed to reassure business leaders that the party would not go soft on Europe if it wins the next general election.
Prime Minister John Major, trailing in opinion polls, must call the election by next May.
"It is absolutely right to sign the social chapter," Brown told BBC radio. Britain now has an opt out to the Social Protocol, or social chapter, of the Maastricht Treaty.
"It is wrong for people to say that a Labour government would remove the requirement of unanimity for changes in social security or for changes in codetermination in the boardroom.
"I'm going to make it absolutely clear today, as has always been clear to the Labour Party, we will veto any attempt to do that," Brown said.
But he added: "An empty chair for Britain is wrong. It is not in Britain's interests because it leaves us disenfranchised."
Brown said it was necessary for workforces to be involved in major decisions in the years to come.
"They have the right to be consulted about what's happening," he said.

Asked if Labour in principle supported a 48-hour working week called for under European Union rules, Brown said: "It is the right of an individual not to have to work for more than 48 hours in certain circumstances where there are not exemptions."

Article 2 of the Social Protocol requires the Council of Ministers to act unanimously in certain areas, including social security, termination of contracts and "collective defence of the interests of workers and employers, including co-determination".
